**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in GRM6 —DISRUPTS→ GRM6 (HGNC:4415); GRM6 (HGNC:4415) —DISRUPTS→ G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007186); G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007186) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital stationary night blindness 1B (MONDO:0009758); Pathogenic variant in TAS2R38 —DISRUPTS→ TAS2R38 (HGNC:11730); TAS2R38 (HGNC:11730) —DISRUPTS→ G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007186); G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007186) —LEADS_TO→ Obsolete thiourea tasting (MONDO:0044248). Similarly, pathogenic variants in TAS2R38 disrupt the same general class of G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathways involved in gustatory perception, leading to obsolete thiourea tasting. Both disease mechanisms converge on the disruption of the shared G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the specific G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathways affected in CSNB1B and obsolete thiourea tasting are topologically and functionally distinct, with no shared downstream effectors or cellular machinery, despite both being GPCR-mediated. _(variant: The identification of common, benign variants in TAS2R38 in populations that do not exhibit the thiourea tasting phenotype, suggesting alternative genetic or environmental factors influence tasting ability.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of GPCR signaling in diverse sensory modalities could reveal novel therapeutic targets for sensory deficits. For example, modulating GPCR signaling pathways might offer avenues for treating certain forms of visual impairment or taste disorders.
